title: Xionites
capsule: The Xionites (Chionites) were a nomadic confederacy of Central Asia first recorded by the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus in 356 CE, when their king Grumbates allied with the Sasanian emperor Shapur II during the siege of Amida. Occupying Transoxiana and Bactria, the Xionites appear to have absorbed or displaced Kushan remnants and are divided by scholars into the Karmir Xyon (Red Huns, associated with the Kidarites and Alchon Huns) and the Spet Xyon (White Huns, the Hephthalites); their exact ethnic and linguistic composition remains debated, with Iranian, Turkic, and Proto-Mongolic elements all proposed. Their political presence in Bactria was extinguished by a coordinated Sasanian-Western Turkic offensive in the 560s, though Nezak remnants persisted into the early seventh century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the narrow 387–402 window in the dataset likely captures a specific phase of Xionite control over portions of Bactria and Transoxiana, but boundaries are scholarly approximations from numismatic and textual evidence.
